sections.h2: Where do I search property records in Collier County, FL?
sections.html:
Begin with the Collier County clerk and comptroller, who keeps the Official Records for the county. The clerk's records search page lists the categories: Official Records (mortgages, deeds, plat maps, condominium declarations and marriage licenses), court records, board minutes, foreclosure judgments, the tax deeds list and Value Adjustment Board files.

The Official Records portal is a separate search tool linked from that page. Search it by party name or document type when you want to see whether a mortgage, lien or earlier deed sits on a Naples, Marco Island or Immokalee property. The clerk's custodian of public records takes requests at 3315 Tamiami Trail East, Suite 102, Naples, FL 34112, phone (239) 252-2646.

sections.h2: What records does the Collier County clerk keep for a house sale?
sections.html:
Every instrument that has to be recorded to protect a buyer ends up in the clerk's Official Records, and a title company searches that file before a Collier County closing. Here is what you will usually find there:

  • Warranty, quit claim and other deeds that moved title to the current owner
  • Mortgages and the satisfactions that release them
  • Plat maps and condominium declarations for the subdivision or building
  • Lis pendens notices filed when a foreclosure case begins

The clerk also posts the foreclosure sale list and the tax deeds list, so a title problem tied to a court case or unpaid tax usually surfaces under one of those headings.

sections.h2: How much does the Collier County clerk charge to record a document?
sections.html:
Naples recording starts at $10.00 for page one of a letter or legal size instrument, then $8.50 per further page, per the clerk's printed schedule. The statute behind the base charge sets $5.00 and $4.00 respectively, and the county page rolls in the extra per-page charges the statute adds. The table below shows the lines most sellers meet.

Collier Clerk recording schedule, from the clerk's fee page
ItemAmount
Recording, first page (letter or legal)$10.00
Recording, each added page$8.50
Plat larger than 8.5 by 14 inches, first page$30.00
Plat, each added page$15.00
Doc stamps on deeds$0.70 per $100.00
Doc stamps on mortgages$0.35 per $100.00
Intangible tax on mortgages$2.00 per $1,000.00
Certification of a document$2.00
Search fee$2.00 per name, instrument or year

Lis pendens recordings carry their own line on that page: $5.00 for the first page, $4.00 for each added page and $1.00 for each name past four. In person, the office takes money orders, cashier's checks, personal checks, cash or cards, and cards add a 3.5% processing fee.

sections.h2: How does documentary stamp tax work on a Collier County deed?
sections.html:
Deeds carry state tax of 70 cents on each $100 of consideration, and the Collier clerk takes the money at the counter or online as the deed goes on record. The clerk's page notes that the amount is rounded up to the nearest hundred.

Under the revenue department's reading, each party to the document answers for the tax, whoever agrees to pay. Consideration takes in cash, a discharged debt and any mortgage on the parcel, assumed or not. Deeds are taxable whether or not they are recorded, and the same page lists warranty, special warranty, quit claim, trustee's and life estate deeds as taxable. The revenue department lists a probate personal representative's deed as not taxable.

Mortgages and notes have their own rates. The state sets 35 cents per $100 of the amount secured, which matches the clerk's mortgage line, and caps the tax on a note at $2,450 with no cap on mortgages. Your closing agent can run the final figure.

Yes, the Collier clerk accepts e-recording through its own sign-in and through partner vendors. Members of the public can register for a public account, submit from a computer, tablet or phone and pay by card, with a 4% fee from the card processor on top of standard recording fees.

  • Scans must be black and white at 300 dpi, on 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 pages.
  • Business customers can open an escrow account funded by electronic transfer, check or cash, with a $0.50 bank fee per transfer up to $75,000.
  • The clerk lists two partner networks and says their services may add processing fees.

A document counts as recorded once the clerk enters it into the Official Records. The office cannot promise same-day recording for mail or electronic submissions, so time-sensitive documents belong at the main office, where they are recorded while you wait.

sections.h2: What should a Collier County owner check in the Official Records before closing?
sections.html:
Pull your own chain of title first, because a clean search saves days at closing. Look up the deed you received, then every instrument recorded against your name since.

  • A mortgage with no recorded satisfaction after payoff
  • Claims of lien from contractors or an owners' association
  • Judgments recorded against a seller with a similar name
  • Recorded easements shown on the plat

The clerk charges $2.00 for a certification and $2.00 for a search per name, instrument or year, so a certified copy of a paid-off mortgage costs little compared with a delayed closing. Heirs selling an inherited house should also ask the clerk's probate division which court file covers the estate, since a personal representative's deed can only follow the court's authority.

sections.h2: How do liens and unpaid taxes show up before a Collier County sale?
sections.html:
Unpaid real estate tax turns into a tax certificate, and its holder can later seek a tax deed that the clerk auctions. The clerk's tax deeds list is the place to see which Collier parcels have reached that stage.

Under state law a tax deed application can be filed after two years have passed since April 1 of the year the certificate was issued. The county tax collector's site links to an online certificate sale. When you sell, gather the collector's payoff and the clerk's lien search side by side and give both to the closing agent. Our Collier County property tax guide covers the billing side.

sections.h2: How do I research a Collier County parcel before listing?
sections.html:
The Collier County Property Appraiser runs the parcel search and posts public data files for the whole county or a smaller area at no charge. Pair a parcel lookup with an Official Records search by owner name, and you can match the legal description on your deed against what the appraiser shows.

Check three things before you list: the owner name spelled the same on the deed and the tax roll, any mortgage with no recorded satisfaction, and any recorded notice from a court case. A mismatch is easier to fix with the clerk before an offer arrives than during the closing week.

faqs.q: Who records deeds in Collier County?
faqs.a: The Collier clerk and comptroller records deeds. The Recording Department is at 3315 Tamiami Trail East, Suite 102, Naples, and takes calls at (239) 252-2646.

faqs.q: What does the Collier clerk charge for the first page of a document?
faqs.a: Page one costs $10.00 and later pages $8.50 each, for letter or legal size instruments. Oversize plats cost $30.00 for page one and $15.00 for every page after.

faqs.q: What is the doc stamp rate on a Collier County deed?
faqs.a: The rate is $0.70 per $100.00 of consideration, rounded up to the nearest hundred on the clerk's schedule. Florida makes all parties to the document liable, so the contract decides who pays it.

faqs.q: Can I use a credit card at the Collier recording desk?
faqs.a: Yes, cards are accepted in person, with a 3.5% processing fee on each transaction. E-recording with a card carries a 4% fee from the card processor.

faqs.q: Will e-recorded documents be recorded the same day?
faqs.a: Not always. The clerk processes mailed and electronic submissions as time permits and cannot guarantee same-day recording, so bring urgent documents to the main office.
